trials.notes: Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment for body-fragment, tree-aware text extraction. Every API call is documented: create_fragment, next_token, get_token_name, is_tag_closer, get_attribute, get_current_depth, get_token_type, get_modifiable_text. The depth-bounded #text walk is the documented pattern and handles decoded href/text, valueless href via is_string(), empty href, and unclosed anchors. Minor near-miss: it uses a nested token loop despite the docs warning that repeated regions can be easier to get wrong with nested cursor walks, though this shape matches the reference and passed cleanly.

Correct processor choice and no undocumented methods: create_fragment, next_token, get_token_type, get_tag, is_tag_closer, get_attribute, get_modifiable_text, get_last_error all appear in the rendered docs. The single-pass state machine follows the documented closer-driven pattern and handles attribute true/null/string semantics and decoded text. Near-misses: returning an empty array on any later get_last_error() is an all-or-nothing read policy that can discard links already parsed before unsupported markup, while the docs leave read-only extraction policy to the caller; also, a stack flushed on closers would output nested A records inner-before-outer if nested anchors were encountered.

Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment and used only documented methods. It applies the key edge rules: is_string() excludes missing and boolean href while preserving empty-string href, get_modifiable_text() is read only for #text tokens, and virtual closers make the unclosed-link case pass. The main weakness is the single $current record: it relies on A closers rather than a depth-bounded subtree walk or stack, and it clears current when any non-string A opener is seen. That is fine for the frozen cases but less robust around nested or foreign-content A elements.

failure_analysis: All three trials passed all 8 frozen cases: simple, no-href-excluded, entity-in-href-decoded, valueless-href, image-link-empty-text, entities-in-text, no-links, and unclosed-link. The docs worked well because they directly surfaced the needed concepts: the Tag Processor "Which processor should I use?" section says to use the HTML Processor for text content and subtree walking; the HTML Processor "Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree" gives the #text-only pattern; get_attribute documents string|true|null semantics and decoded attribute values; get_modifiable_text documents decoded #text and warns not to treat all modifiable text as DOM text; next_token/get_current_depth explain virtual closers and the >= depth boundary that make unclosed anchors work. The near-misses were not hidden-test failures: trial-2 chose an all-or-nothing get_last_error policy that differs from the reference's best-effort prefix behavior on unsupported markup after a parsed link, and trials 2/3 would be shaky if nested A tokens appear in foreign or invalid markup because their closer-driven state is not explicitly ordered by opener document position.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::get_last_error and the read-only extraction guidance in "Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree"
doc_gaps.problem: The docs say read-only callers choose whether to return accumulated data or reject, but they do not make the consequences concrete for array extractors. A model reasonably returned [] on any later parser abort, discarding already-parsed records.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general note or small table contrasting best-effort prefix extraction with all-or-nothing extraction: get_last_error() means the scan ended early, not that previously visited tokens are invalid; choose and document the function's policy.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::next_token, "There is only ONE cursor" warning
doc_gaps.problem: The docs warn against nested token loops for repeated regions, while nearby subtree examples use a bounded inner loop. The distinction is subtle.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify when a bounded inner subtree walk is acceptable and what token the processor is left on after the loop, versus when repeated sibling regions should use a single state-machine loop.

doc_gaps.problem: The DT example demonstrates flushing on closers, but not how to preserve document-order records for nested matching elements or attribute-qualified elements.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general pattern for collecting repeated element records: create the record at the qualifying opener for document order, accumulate while active, and flush/update on the matching closer; note when a stack is needed and when nested matches are impossible or parser-normalized.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor method section lists string|true|null but is less explicit than the Tag Processor section about decoded string values. Subjects had both files, but the subclass section should stand alone.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Repeat or explicitly inherit the decoded attribute-value contract: string values are already character-reference decoded, true means valueless boolean attribute, null means unavailable.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment / HTML Support / next_token incomplete-token notes
doc_gaps.problem: Factory failure, unsupported parser abort, trailing incomplete syntax, and virtual closers are documented in separate places, making edge-policy decisions harder.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact parser-state decision table: create_fragment() null, next_token() false with paused_at_incomplete_token(), get_last_error() non-null, and normal virtual closers for unclosed elements, with what each means for already-visited tokens.
